question: If P, F and C represent respectively the pole, principal focus and centre of curvature of a concave mirror, then PC will be equal to.
solution:
The correct answer is __**2PF**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• For a concave mirror, the distance between the pole (P) and the centre of curvature (C) is known as the radius of curvature (R).
 
• The principal focus (F) is the point where parallel rays of light either converge or appear to diverge after reflecting from the mirror.
 
• The distance between the pole (P) and the principal focus (F) is known as the focal length (f).
 
• In a concave mirror, the radius of curvature (R) is twice the focal length (f), thus PC = 2PF.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pole (P):** The pole is the geometric center of the mirror's surface. It is the point where the principal axis meets the mirror.
 
• **Principal Focus (F):** The principal focus is the point on the principal axis of a concave or convex mirror where parallel rays of light, after reflection, either converge (concave) or appear to diverge (convex).
 
• **Centre of Curvature (C):** The centre of curvature is the point on the principal axis which is the center of the sphere of which the mirror is a part. For a concave mirror, it lies in front of the mirror.
 
• **Radius of Curvature (R):** The radius of curvature is the distance between the pole (P) and the centre of curvature (C). It is twice the focal length (f) of the mirror.
 
• **Focal Length (f):** The focal length is the distance between the pole (P) and the principal focus (F). It is half of the radius of curvature (R).
